security_audit.summary: The Python helper makes outbound HTTPS requests to public Ensembl REST endpoints. This is expected, but sensitive genomic queries can leave the local environment. The shell execution and reconnaissance findings are documentation false positives, and no prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound Ensembl API requests can expose sensitive genomic queries.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external network dependency and warn users not to send identifiable patient data without approval.

remediation.issue: Endpoint path values are built from user-supplied species, gene, variant, and region inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Validate or URL-encode path segments before sending requests to reduce malformed request and logging risks.

remediation.issue: Optional installation examples use unpinned package names.
remediation.suggestion: Document trusted package sources and consider version pins for reproducible research environments.

content.value_statement: Genomic research needs reliable gene, sequence, variant, and homology data from one source. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Ensembl REST API workflows.
actual_capabilities: Look up genes by symbol, Ensembl ID, or external database reference.
Retrieve genomic, transcript, coding, protein, FASTA, or JSON sequence data.
Analyze variants by rsID or HGVS notation using Ensembl VEP endpoints.
Find orthologs, paralogs, gene trees, and cross-species homology records.
Map coordinates between assemblies such as GRCh37 and GRCh38.
List supported species and retrieve assembly metadata for a chosen species.
limitations: It requires internet access to Ensembl public REST servers.
It does not provide clinical interpretation or medical advice.
Results depend on Ensembl availability, release data, and rate limits.
It does not include a local cache or offline database.

use_cases.title: Annotate A Candidate Gene
use_cases.description: Retrieve gene coordinates, transcripts, identifiers, and external references for a research target.

use_cases.title: Review Variant Consequences
use_cases.description: Use Ensembl variation and VEP endpoints to summarize predicted effects and population data.

use_cases.title: Compare Species Homology
use_cases.description: Find orthologs and paralogs across selected species for comparative genomics planning.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up A Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Ensembl database skill to look up BRCA2 in human. Summarize its Ensembl ID, location, transcripts, and external references.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve A Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the genomic sequence for ENSG00000139618 from Ensembl. Provide FASTA output and mention the assembly used.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze A Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Query Ensembl for rs699 in human. Summarize variant location, alleles, population frequencies, and predicted consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Comparative Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a workflow to compare BRCA2 orthologs in human, mouse, and zebrafish using Ensembl. Include endpoints, expected outputs, and rate-limit handling.

output_examples.output: A concise gene summary with the Ensembl gene ID, chromosome location, strand, transcript count, and key external database links.
A variant report listing genomic location, observed alleles, transcript consequences, predicted impact terms, and population frequency notes.

output_examples.input: Find mouse orthologs for human BRCA2.
output_examples.output: A homology summary with target species, ortholog identifiers, gene names, relationship type, and confidence notes.

best_practices: Specify species, assembly, and Ensembl release when reproducibility matters.
Use batch endpoints, caching, and rate-limit handling for repeated queries.
Review privacy rules before sending sensitive genomic or patient-linked data.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Ensembl annotations as clinical diagnosis or treatment guidance.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates without explicit assembly mapping.
Do not run large one-by-one queries when a batch endpoint is available.

faq.question: What Ensembl data can this skill help retrieve?
faq.answer: It can help retrieve genes, sequences, variants, homology records, regulatory features, species data, and assembly information.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No. The documented Ensembl REST API workflows use public anonymous access, subject to rate limits.

faq.question: Can it work with GRCh37 coordinates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents the GRCh37 Ensembl REST host and assembly mapping workflows.

faq.question: Can it analyze clinical significance?
faq.answer: No. It can retrieve annotations and predicted consequences, but clinical interpretation needs qualified review.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users avoid sending?
faq.answer: Users should avoid sending identifiable patient data or sensitive research data unless their policy allows external API use.
